country.comment: Study was conducted in rural Cambodia, specifically across 30 villages in four districts of Kampong Chhnang province in the Tonle Sap Lake region.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title and Abstract; PDF p. 4, Methods (Sampling frame and sample size); PDF p. 7, Results; PDF p. 9, Limitations

effect_estimate.comment: Quantitative experimental estimates from household-level logistic regression (with village-clustered standard errors) and village-level OLS regressions, supplemented by market-distortion and cost-effectiveness analyses. Note that sales conversions reflect latrine orders rather than verified installations.
effect_estimate.value: Being offered a 50% targeted sanitation subsidy increased the predicted probability of latrine purchase among eligible households by 31.3 percentage points (marginal probability = 0.313, p = 0.00; reported as 31 percentage points in text) compared with ineligible control households, whereas eligible control (0.0132, p = 0.416) and ineligible treatment (0.0056, p = 0.860) households did not differ significantly from baseline. In treatment villages, the sales closing rate was 38% among subsidy-eligible households versus 6% among ineligible households (p = 0.00), and overall sales conversions were 22% in treatment areas versus 7% in control areas (p = 0.00; 437 total latrines sold: 326 treatment, 111 control). At the village level, offering subsidies increased overall village latrine closing rates by 23 percentage points (p = 0.00) and increased purchase rates among subsidy-qualifying households by 32 percentage points / 32% (p = 0.00), including a 37 percentage point increase among Poverty Probability Index (PPI)-qualifying households (p = 0.00) and a 26% increase among IDPoor-qualifying households (p = 0.03). Direct household climate vulnerability increased the subsidy effect by an additional 10 percentage points over baseline (p = 0.00), with no statistically significant market distortion among ineligible households (only 3 of 2,352 non-purchasing households cited waiting for a subsidy).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract and Highlights; PDF p. 6, Results and Table 1; PDF p. 7, Results

mechanism_certainty.comment: Experimental evidence from a village-level cluster-randomized controlled trial directly testing a two-layer socioeconomic and climate-vulnerability subsidy targeting mechanism on household latrine purchase. Authors note potential minor post-randomization targeting differences (51–52% eligible in treatment vs. 45% in control, driven by a 5% higher share of IDPoor households identified in treatment villages, p = 0.00) and measurement of orders rather than final installations.

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines a two-layer targeted subsidy eligibility screening mechanism combining government IDPoor status, a 10-question Poverty Probability Index (PPI) assessment, and commune/household climate vulnerability thresholds (ELIGIBILITY, hardship_exception, accommodation), 50% purchase-price discounts addressing latrine cost barriers (BURDEN, fees), field eligibility screening and spot-check procedures integrated into door-to-door visits (procedural_steps), and active outreach/identification by trained iDE sales agents and village authorities (DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, bureaucratic_assistance).

outcome_flags.comment: Primary outcome is purchase/uptake of durable, climate-resilient household latrines (Easy Latrine and elevated Sky Latrine) among rural households without a toilet (sanitation_access), alongside financial affordability via 50% retail price discounts and unit cost/cost-effectiveness analysis (affordability).

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Primary causal evaluation is a cluster-randomized controlled trial in which treatment status (availability of targeted 50% sanitation subsidies) was randomly assigned at the village (cluster) level across 30 villages stratified by climate vulnerability, with supplementary stakeholder interviews (n = 13) and programmatic cost analysis used to assess market distortion and scalability.
risk_of_bias_tool.where_found: PDF p. 2, Introduction; PDF p. 4–5, Methods (Sampling frame and sample size; Data analysis)

sample_size.comment: Power calculation required at least 26 villages (2,600 households); final quantitative sample comprised 30 villages (15 treatment, 15 control; 23 climate-vulnerable villages: 12 treatment, 11 control) across four districts in Kampong Chhnang province, with 2,821 unique household sales presentations after dropping 1,598 duplicate visits (resulting in 437 latrine sales and 2,352 non-purchasing households). Qualitative component comprised 13 in-depth stakeholder interviews.
sample_size.value: 30 villages (15 treatment, 15 control) and 2,821 unique household sales presentations (quantitative); 13 in-depth interviews with latrine business owners, local government representatives, and sales agents (qualitative)
